policy.publicRule: Only publish source-approved public operational information, aggregate needs, and redacted outputs.
policy.privateRule: Use exact reports, partner operational data, and sensitive context only in role-gated coordination views.
policy.aiRule: AI-derived labels, geocodes, summaries, and urgency scores are advisory metadata requiring human validation.

sources.licenseReview: CC BY 4.0 and ODbL options; includes Copernicus Sentinel-2-derived data. Attribute Google Research and respect Earth Engine/Cloud export limits.
sources.coverage: Africa, South Asia, South-East Asia, Latin America, and the Caribbean, including Venezuela.
sources.access: Earth Engine ImageCollection and Google Cloud Storage export workflow for selected areas of interest.

sources.name: EOX Sentinel-2 Cloudless 2024 national imagery for Venezuela
sources.owner: EOX IT Services GmbH / Copernicus Sentinel-2
sources.recommendedUse: Open, shareable Venezuela-wide optical context for the default map. Use for regional and city-scale visual orientation only; 10 m Sentinel-2 imagery cannot confirm individual building damage and must not be upscaled into evidence claims.
sources.licenseReview: EOxCloudless requires attribution to EOxCloudless / EOX IT Services GmbH and notes that it contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024. Review the current EOX terms before redistribution beyond public map visualization.
sources.beforeScene: Annual 2024 Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic, not a pre-earthquake event scene.
sources.afterScene: Annual 2024 Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic, not a post-earthquake event scene.
sources.access: Public EOX WMTS tiles in Web Mercator, used as the default national satellite context. Maximum useful native visual zoom is 14 for the Sentinel-2 cloudless layer; the public app caps national-only zoom there instead of presenting overzoomed tiles as building-scale evidence.

sources.name: 2026 Venezuela earthquake: AI building and damage assessment
sources.recommendedUse: Multi-area AI-derived and human-validated damage context for Caracas, Caraballeda, Catia La Mar, La Guaira, Moron, and Naiguata. Use for prioritization and visualization, not as verified household-level damage.
sources.licenseReview: Review the dataset card and per-area source files before redistribution. Damage comes from HOTOSM fAIr, Microsoft AI for Good Lab, OSU/CUNY Sentinel-1, and MapSwipe validation depending on area.
sources.coverage: Six affected-area AOIs plus validated overview files for the 24 June 2026 Venezuela earthquake.
sources.access: Public Hugging Face dataset. The app caches a small AOI/count summary into public/data/hotosm-venezuela-damage-areas.geojson.

sources.name: Vantor high-resolution pre/post imagery for Catia La Mar
sources.owner: Vantor Open Data STAC, cataloged by NASA Earthdata GIS
sources.recommendedUse: Building-scale before/after source context for the Catia La Mar damage viewer. Use one LG02 7 Apr 2026 pre-event Vantor Open Data STAC COG and one LG05 27 Jun 2026 post-event Vantor Open Data STAC COG in a strict shared footprint. Do not stack LG02/LG04/LG06 fill scenes in the public slider because mixed optical footprints can create repeated-looking buildings, scale changes, and tone seams. Do not infer individual damage labels without Microsoft/HDX assessment and human validation.
sources.licenseReview: NASA Earthdata GIS item points to the external Vantor STAC catalog. Vantor Open Data event imagery is attributed in-app as CC BY-NC 4.0. Attribute Vantor and NASA catalog context; avoid commercial derivative use without separate review.
sources.afterScene: Post-event imagery: Vantor LG05 Image B15000110186C610, acquired 2026-06-27, approximately 0.349 m GSD, bbox [-67.043108, 10.524025, -66.942944, 10.642557].
sources.access: NASA Earthdata GIS catalog record with external Vantor STAC. The public slider loads one LG02 7 Apr 2026 pre-event COG and one LG05 27 Jun 2026 post-event COG through HOTOSM TiTiler only when the comparison is enabled, clips both layers to their strict shared footprint, and keeps EOX Sentinel-2 Cloudless underneath as a low-priority open national visual underlay outside the true pre/post overlap.

sources.name: Line of Sight Surface Displacement Map on 6/25/2026 (NISAR) for the Venezuela Earthquakes
sources.owner: NASA-JPL/Caltech Team, NISAR Operations Science Team
sources.recommendedUse: Public surface-displacement context for the earthquake response. Use to understand broad deformation patterns; do not interpret as building-level structural damage or calibrated ground truth.
sources.licenseReview: NASA Earth Science data are generally open, but this item is experimental/research-grade. Use with NASA-JPL/Caltech attribution and include the item's modified Copernicus Sentinel data notice where applicable.
sources.afterScene: NISAR post-event image acquired 2026-06-25; line-of-sight displacement map at 80 m posting
sources.access: NASA Earthdata GIS ArcGIS ImageServer exportImage overlay loaded only when the NASA/NISAR layer is enabled.

sources.name: Sentinel-1 Likelihood of Damaged Structures (Experimental) for the Venezuela Earthquake June 2026
sources.owner: NASA Disasters Response Coordination System / Oregon State University
sources.recommendedUse: Experimental Sentinel-1 coherent-change damage-likelihood context across the affected region. Use for situational awareness and review prioritization only; do not publish as a verified building-by-building census.
sources.licenseReview: Preliminary, unvalidated rapid assessment. Attribute the Sentinel-1 damage analysis authors and Overture Maps building footprints; preserve NASA item caveats.
sources.afterScene: Sentinel-1 post-event swaths from 2026-06-24 22:49 UTC and 2026-06-25 10:16 UTC
sources.access: NASA Earthdata GIS web map and public ArcGIS FeatureServer; not loaded by default in the public viewer to avoid rendering millions of building polygons.
